brief: Samuel Azariah was born in 1874 near the southern tip of India. As a young man he was a YMCA evangelist. He became a missionary and then in 1912 the first Indian Anglican bishop. He served the Diocese of Dornakal for over thirty years, during which it grew rapidly. Azariah brought to world missionary and ecumenical conferences his vision that missions should be set free to grow into responsible indigenous churches. He was among those instrumental in the forming of the Church of South India, which finally came into being in 1947, two years after his death.
